goal: task-worker.sh runs each task in its own .workflow/worktrees/<task-id>/ git worktree on branch flywheel/<phase>/<task-id>, FF-only-merges to the worker's starting branch on lifecycle.status=done, parks the worktree on failed/interrupted/uncommitted-changes-at-DONE, and runs a 7-day retention sweep at startup -- replacing the LKG-routed invocation inside the worker.

references: .workflow/task-worker.sh:116-122 -- run_workflow helper that routes through .workflow/lkg/; rewrite to invoke flywheel from the live tree and pass --sandbox <worktree-path>
.workflow/task-worker.sh:184-194 -- current --sandbox $REPO_ROOT line; replace with per-task worktree path
src/flywheel/workflow.py:433-444 -- existing SIGINT handler that finalizes interrupted lifecycles (relied on, unchanged)
constraints: Worktree path is .workflow/worktrees/<task-id>/ and branch name is flywheel/<phase>/<task-id>, where <phase> is the task file's parent directory name under .workflow/tasks/active/. If the task file lives directly under .workflow/tasks/active/ with no phase subdir, fall back to flywheel/_root/<task-id>.
Phase base is the branch the worker started on (typically main); record it once at startup. Each new worktree branches off the live tip of phase base at creation time (post-merge of any prior task).

On lifecycle.status=done with a clean worktree (`git status --porcelain` empty) and >0 commits on the task branch: `git merge --ff-only flywheel/<phase>/<task-id>` from phase base. On FF failure, `git rebase <base>` the task branch once and retry FF. On rebase failure, `git rebase --abort`, leave the worktree intact, log the path, continue the worker loop.

On lifecycle.status=done with uncommitted changes (any porcelain output, including untracked files) in the worktree: do not auto-commit, do not merge, leave the worktree on its branch, log a clear line naming the worktree path. Treat as a per-iteration failure that does not block the worker.

On lifecycle.status=done with zero commits on the task branch (`git rev-list --count <base>..<branch>` == 0): no-op merge -- remove the worktree via `git worktree remove`, delete the branch via `git branch -d`, leave phase base unchanged, log `no commits to merge`.
On lifecycle.status in (failed, interrupted): preserve the worktree and the branch. No merge attempt. Worker proceeds to next iteration.

Worker startup runs a retention sweep before entering the main loop: `git worktree prune` first to clean dangling entries, then remove `.workflow/worktrees/*` directories whose mtime is older than `--worktree-retention-days` days (default 7) and `git branch -D` the matching `flywheel/<phase>/<id>` branch. mkdir -p .workflow/worktrees/ if missing.

Worktree-creation failure (disk full, branch collision, dirty index, path already exists, etc.) exits the wrapper non-zero BEFORE invoking `python -m flywheel.workflow run`. No lifecycle row, no harness.* event. The worker's eligibility loop reselects the same task next iteration.

The wrapper reads the terminal lifecycle.status for the just-finished run from .workflow/flywheel.sqlite via the `sqlite3` CLI (most recent lifecycle row for the task_id). Use the same DB_PATH variable the worker already exposes.

Remove the LKG bootstrap block (lines 99-106), the LKG_DIR and PROMOTE_SCRIPT variables, the `[worker] LKG : ...` log line, and the `uv run --project "$LKG_DIR"` invocation in run_workflow. Route flywheel through `uv run python -m flywheel.workflow ...` from the repo root.

Document --worktree-retention-days in `task-worker.sh --help` and reframe --sandbox documentation: it is now overridden per-task by the worktree, so the --sandbox flag is effectively unused. Remove --sandbox from the worker's CLI surface, or leave it as a no-op with a note; choose whichever keeps the diff smaller.

Helper structure is an authoring choice: one helper or several (e.g. .workflow/worktree-create.sh, worktree-merge.sh, worktree-sweep.sh). All helpers live in `.workflow/`. No new Python module. `set -euo pipefail` and `bash -n` clean.
Commit the change with a Conventional Commits message (feat:) before reporting verify.
non_goals: Do not edit any file under src/flywheel/ -- strategy-layer work only per docs/strategy.md and the spec's 'Zero changes to src/flywheel/' guarantee.
Do not delete .workflow/lkg/, .workflow/promote-lkg.sh, or docs/lkg.md, and do not update LKG references in docs/strategy.md or CLAUDE.md. The follow-up task `remove-lkg` does that mop-up.
Do not update the 'LKG snapshot' code comments at src/flywheel/store_sqlite.py:55 and src/flywheel/store_postgres.py:69 -- they sit inside src/flywheel/ which is out of scope.
Do not add multi-worker locking, remote push, PR creation, or harness.blocked auto-unblock logic.
Do not introduce a Python helper for any of this work; bash + sqlite3 CLI + git only.
Do not add a verify-precheck grader or any change to grader execution order -- that is parked future work.
edge_cases: Stale worktree directory from a prior worker death blocks `git worktree add` for the same task id. The startup sweep + `git worktree prune` clears it; until then, worktree-creation fails fast (FR-10 path) and the operator sees the path in the log.
Operator manually deleted the worktree dir but kept the branch: `git worktree prune` during sweep cleans the dangling worktree entry; next `git worktree add` succeeds.

Two tasks across different phases share the same task id: branch names differ (`flywheel/<phaseA>/<id>` vs `flywheel/<phaseB>/<id>`) but `.workflow/worktrees/<task-id>/` collides -- treat the second as worktree-creation failure; operator resolves.

SIGINT mid-task: src/flywheel/workflow.py:433-444 already finalizes the lifecycle as `interrupted`; the wrapper observes that status on next read and parks the worktree. No new SIGINT handling needed in the wrapper.
Untracked files in the worktree at DONE count as uncommitted state (FR-8 fail-loud). `git status --porcelain` reports them; do not filter.
Phase base advanced between worktree creation and DONE (e.g. an earlier task merged): FF would fail; the wrapper rebases the task branch onto current base once, then retries FF.
Task whose agent reaches DONE without committing: no-op merge path. Worktree removed, branch deleted, phase base unchanged, log notes 'no commits to merge'.
